citations.text: The paragraph identifies 工 as a pictograph resembling a carpenter’s square used to draw right angles or squares. It says an early end-frame contracted to a horizontal stroke by late Shang, while earlier Western Zhou bronze forms retained a thick lower stroke. The author proposes 矩 (a carpenter’s square) as the original referent, then presents craft worker as an early extension, with further extensions to skill and engineering; it traces 功績 from engineering and official/administrative senses from craft or engineering. These are this author’s proposed graphic and semantic account, not an independently established chronology. The page also cites the Western Zhou 伊簋 and the Analects for craft-worker senses, and reports a Western Zhou 金文 title written as an unresolved glyph followed by 工, conventionally written 司空 in transmitted texts.
